text:
jordana: Quick question  I've already got payroll set to 6% pre-tax for 401k. I want to bump to 10% starting asap. If I submit a change now, will it hit the next paycheck or do I miss the cutoff? Also, I'm 52 so planning catch-up contributions Do I need a separate form for that, or is it in the same change? And does increasing HSA deferral reduce the 401k % (i.e., is it dollar-limited or percent-of-pay)?

marco (People Ops): Hey @jordana  good questions. Short answers: 1) Depends on payroll cutoff for the upcoming cycle, 2) catch-up (50+) is a separate election but can usually be done in the same benefits portal flow, and 3) 401k % is applied to gross base eligible pay, independent of HSA elections.

jordana: Cool, thanks. What is the cutoff date exactly for the 04/15 pay?

payroll-bot: Payroll reminder: For the 04/15 payroll, deferral changes must be submitted by 04/07 23:59 PT to be effective on 04/15. Changes after that are queued for the following pay period.

amy (Finance): Adding: if you change from 6% to 10% mid-cycle (after cutoff) we can't retroactively take the higher percentage for the earlier portion of that pay period without a manual adjustment, which we only do for legitimate missed elections (not for routine increases). Manual retro can affect year-to-date withholding and will generate an off-cycle payroll entry.

marco (People Ops): To enroll catch-up: open Benefits Portal -> Retirement -> Update Contribution. There's a checkbox for "Age 50+ catch-up" and a numeric field for catch-up amount (dollars). If you prefer forms, upload the completed form: "403b-401k-deferral-change.pdf" (we accept signed PDFs).

jordana: Is the catch-up expressed as dollar amount or percent? I want to make sure I don't hit contribution limits.

amy (Finance): Catch-up is a dollar amount (IRS limit for 2026 is $8,000 for 50+; double check the portal header for current year). The portal will show an estimate of projected annual contributions after you set percent + catch-up.

jordana: And HSA pretax = taken out of gross before tax, so that doesn't lower the 401k percent base, right? If I put 5% to HSA and 10% to 401k, payroll will still take 10% of gross for 401k?

marco (People Ops): Correct. 401k percent is calculated on eligible gross wages and is not reduced by HSA pre-tax elections. The only thing that impacts 401k baseline is pre-tax transportation or commuter deductions if those are set to a specific taxable wage base in our payroll config (rare).

jordana: Great. One more: I clicked update in the portal and it said "Change submitted  pending vendor acceptance". How long does vendor acceptance usually take?

benefits-portal-bot: Benefits Portal: Change 0x9c7d submitted. Vendor ACK expected within 2 business days. If vendor rejects, People Ops will reach out with the rejection reason.

marco (People Ops): Usually 24-48 hours. If vendor ACK hasn't come through and you're close to cutoff, DM me the portal change ID and we can do a manual override/email to vendor. If you need it on the immediate next paycheck and the portal vendor hasn't ACKed, manually emailing a signed deferral change PDF to hr-benefits@redwood.com with employee ID (last 4) will ensure payroll can pick it up pre-cutoff.

jordana: Awesome, thanks y'all. I'll set the portal to 10% + $6k catch-up and watch for ACK. :slightly_smiling_face:

amy (Finance): One last note: if you're changing Roth vs pre-tax allocation, that matters for tax withholding but not the percent cap. Portal will let you split pre-tax and Roth by percentage if desired.

marco (People Ops): Thanks @jordana. If anyone else has similar questions about mid-period changes or catch-up elections, I'm happy to run a short doc or quick FAQ to put in the benefits guide.

jordana: Please do  that would help!
